headline: S&P 500 earnings momentum remains strong with 20%+ growth expected for second consecutive quarter, supporting equity market thesis
reasoning: Talevski argues that earnings momentum is the strongest force behind equity markets and has not been seen at this level in a very long time. S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow above 20% for the second consecutive quarter for Q2, with semiconductor earnings above 50% being key. The S&P 500 is trading at a forward 23x one-year PE, just slightly above the long-term average but not overly expensive. Market breadth is also improving, with 70% of stocks trading above their 200-day moving average, and strength spreading beyond the Magnificent Seven.
quote: we haven't seen earnings momentum like this in a very, very long time. And that still remains the strong kind of force behind equity markets. And you know S&P 500 earnings are expected to grow above 20% for the second consecutive quarter for Q2 above 50%. Obviously the semiconductor earnings remain the key there. And look, even you know, S&P 500 is currently trading at forward 23 times one year PE, which is just a little bit above that long term average. But it's reasonable. It's not overly expensive. So I think there are some of the factors. Regardless that I think the earnings momentum is still going to drive markets going forward.

headline: Australian equity market's recent record run seen as a catch-up rally rather than a surprise, with FY2026 local earnings still looking strong in mid-teens
reasoning: Talevski explains that Australian equity markets have actually outperformed global equities in the last couple of months, but frames this as a catch-up rally. At end of June, Aussie equities were up around 7-9% versus global equities up 13% and hedged returns up in the 20s. He notes FY2026 local earnings are still looking pretty strong in the mid-teens, making the resilience understandable rather than truly surprising.
quote: in the last couple of months alone, I think from memory, they have actually helped perform global equity. So it's been sort of more of a catch up rally because I mean, let's face it, at the end of June, I think equity Aussie equity markets were up about, you know, 8 or 9% or 7%. Actually global equity markets were up 13 and hedge was up, up in the 20s. So I could see that more as a catch up rally rather than the surprise. And look even said of the financial year 2026 for for local earnings is still looking pretty strong in the sort of mid-teens.

headline: AI theme remains intact following hyperscaler earnings, though increasingly dependent on capital markets for financing
reasoning: Talevski says the July AI jitters have passed, with hyperscaler earnings and subsequent price action confirming the AI story is still well and truly alive. Financing and deal announcements have further validated this. However, the AI theme is increasingly dependent on capital markets, which represents a key risk. AI is expected to have a meaningful impact on GDP growth and productivity, continuing to support equity markets.
quote: You know, we've got through the July AI jitters, hyperscalers earnings and sort of that price reaction since has shown sort of that's sort of behind us. Um, financing and deal announcements confirmed that, you know, AI and the story is still well and truly, um, alive, but it's increasingly dependent on capital markets. And that's the risk.

headline: Activam expects a 10-15% market drawdown in the next couple of months despite strong fundamentals, but remains positioned for growth
reasoning: Talevski expects a drawdown of around 10-15% in the next couple of months even with fundamentals and earnings remaining strong. Sources of near-term volatility include the new Fed framework that markets are still adjusting to, and share unlock events. Despite this, he believes bull markets are likely to see another run for at least another year, supported by AI's impact on GDP and productivity and broadening strength across small, mid, and large caps.

Although we still think that probably we will see a bit of a down, a drawdown in the next set, a couple of months in that sort of 10 to 15%, even with fundamentals and earnings where they are. That's also um you know a source for volatility. But look bull markets um, you know likely to see another bull run for at least another year. Obviously AI and you know that meaningful kind of impact on GDP growth and productivity that's really going to continue to sort of support markets.

headline: Activam overweight global equities, global small caps, emerging markets and credit over domestic equities
reasoning: Talevski states that Activam continues to be overweight global equities over domestic, as well as global small caps, emerging markets, and credit. He believes there is still upside to come from these sectors. The broadening of strength across small caps and mid caps alongside large caps should continue to power equity markets.
quote: in terms of our positioning, we continue to be sort of overweight global equities over domestic global small caps and emerging markets and credit. And we still feel that there's still some upside to come out of these sectors.

headline: 10-year US bond yields approaching 4.8% threshold that has historically triggered equity market volatility and potential pullback
reasoning: Robert Talevski notes that US 10-year yields are sitting around 4.77% and approaching a critical level where they compete with corporate debt and equity returns. A break above 4.8% is the level that historically has stopped markets in their tracks. September tends to be a difficult period for stocks, and with midterms approaching, the last two midterm cycles both saw significant turbulence. Despite this, earnings momentum remains a strong force behind equity markets.
quote: ten year yields are sitting at around 4.77. You know, we are approaching a point where yields are climbing to a level where they sort of compete with corporate debt. And equity returns are, a break above 4.8% is the level that triggers the volatility. As history tells us, 4.8% plus yield ten year bond yields has stopped markets in their tracks. Um, September itself tends to be a difficult period for stocks with midterms approaching. If you look at the last two midterm cycles, both saw real sort of turbulence.
